title: Extension methods and C# 14 extension members
hook: Redis cache-key helpers used to be this-string methods. In C# 14 they can be extension properties and even static members that look like they live on the type.

sections.heading: Classic this-parameter methods still exist
sections.prose: An extension method is a static method in a non-nested, non-generic static class whose first parameter is marked this. Callers write instance syntax; the compiler emits a static call. LINQ’s Where and Select are the canonical example: they appear on IEnumerable<T> after using System.Linq. Extensions never pierce encapsulation. If the type already has a matching instance member, that member wins. Namespace-level using imports every extension in that namespace, not one class.

snippets.label: Classic this-method for a cache key
snippets.explanation: Readable at the call site. Still a static method; RedisKeyExtensions.AsAttemptKey(attemptId, "acme") is identical IL.

sections.heading: C# 14 extension blocks: methods, properties, static members
sections.prose: C# 14, shipping with .NET 10, adds extension member blocks. Inside a static class you write extension(ReceiverType name) { ... } for instance-like members, including properties. A second form, extension(ReceiverType) with no receiver name, declares static-looking members on the type: static methods, static properties, and operators. Microsoft’s What’s new in C# 14 sample extends IEnumerable<T> with IsEmpty, Combine, Identity, and operator +. Bind order does not change: instance members of the type still beat extensions. ref on the receiver is how struct extensions mutate in place. Prefer real type members when you own the source; use extensions when you do not, or when the behavior is layer-specific.

snippets.label: C# 14 extension property and static type member
snippets.explanation: AttemptCacheKey is invoked like an instance property. SessionPrefix is invoked like a static property of string. Neither exists on System.String itself.

interviewTakeaways: this-methods: instance-looking static methods, methods only.
C# 14 extension { }: instance and static members, including properties and operators.
Both compile to static calls; real instance members always win.
ref receivers mutate structs; by-value receivers copy.
commonPitfalls: Expecting an extension to override a type’s own method.
Forgetting using of the namespace so the member vanishes from IntelliSense.
Mutating a struct through a by-value extension and wondering why the local is unchanged.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS can assign Array.prototype.foo and change every array. C# extensions are compile-time sugar; they do not patch the type for other languages or reflection as instance members.
TypeScript can merge interfaces to add methods at the type level; implementation is still a runtime assignment. C# 14 extensions are implemented by the compiler as static members.
